newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end quiet range-trade firmer.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end quiet range-trade firmer.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures posted small gains after a session of quiet range-trading.
March yen rose again late when a big fund bought, but traders said activity in most other pits stayed subdued.
"The mark and Swiss franc had a really muted, really terrible (volume) day," said one floor broker.

Traders tied the drop-off in turnover from Friday's busy pace to a market turned hesitant after the weekend Group of Seven meeting in Berlin. They said the G7's short statement suggested the dollar's strong, rapid rally might slow to a grind but is unlikely to screech to a halt.

The G7 said major misalignments in exchange markets, noted in its April 1995 communique, have been corrected. It reaffirmed its view that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility is undesirable.
"It (G7) kind of put the brakes on it (dollar) for now," said a floor broker. "But everybody's still short currencies."
Some brokers also noted that the G7 did not specifically mention intervention, and British and German officials said the G7 did not weigh the matter of coordinated intervention.

Sterling expanded gains, however, as traders compared Britain's economy to others in Europe and decided the pound still looked inviting to buyers as they waited for Wednesday's quarterly inflation report from the Bank of England.
Some expected U.K. inflation to heat up enough to overshoot targets and pave the way for higher rates.
"Sterling looks terrific," the first floor broker said. "Theirs is the one European country doing well."
March Canadian dollar, after nearing an intraday objective at $0.7422, slipped to the 200-day moving average at $0.7396.

March yen rose $0.000017 to $0.008190, marks firmed $0.0009 to $0.6053, Swiss francs rose $0.0017 to $0.7038, sterling jumped $0.0108 to $1.6408, the Canadian dollar lost $0.0027 to $0.7401, Aussie dollar fell $0.0028 to $0.7578, and the Mexican peso rose $0.000325 to $0.126275.
